**Subject: Re: Saturday alarm**

Hi Kristen,

Here’s my account of what happened Saturday.

At about 10:40, I put a bag of butter popcorn in the break-room microwave, pressed the popcorn button, and went back out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and helping him took longer than I expected—maybe six or seven minutes. By the time I got back, the store had cleared out. The engine from Hertel arrived about 25 minutes later. Thankfully, there was no damage—just smoke and a burnt-popcorn smell.

It was my popcorn, and it was my mistake. The microwave didn’t do anything wrong; I left it unattended. The September alarm wasn’t me—that was the paint-aisle sensor—but I know that doesn’t make Saturday any less of a mess. I’m sorry the customers had to stand outside in the cold, and I feel bad about the Hendersons leaving their full cart.

I’ve been on the job 31 years, and my first alarm as a civilian was over a bag of butter popcorn. My wife says the van smelled like a burnt movie theater. I’m sure Mikey Szymanski, who I broke in as a probie back in ’03, will remind me of it for years.

I’ll cover the $175 dispatch charge. You can take it out of my check, or I can bring in cash—your call. I’ll buy Denise her coffee, too.

I’d really like to keep my Saturday shifts. I enjoy the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I understand Gary’s concern, and I’ll make sure this doesn’t happen again.

Walt

reasons: The request says the store was cleared out for about 25 minutes, but the piece says the engine arrived about 25 minutes later, which changes the stated timeline.
